items.title: Altman says OpenAI now publishes its pretraining progress
items.takeaway: Sam Altman calls OpenAI's new transparency into its pretraining progress 'the most important thing' in a while and hopes labs agree to common limits.
items.soWhat: If labs adopt common limits, the pace of frontier model releases becomes easier to predict.

items.title: Patrick Collison says agentic commerce is growing extremely quickly
items.takeaway: Patrick Collison posted that agentic commerce is growing extremely quickly, with a chart. Stratechery also covered agentic commerce on Nov 19.
items.soWhat: Purchases made by agents for customers are becoming a sales channel worth planning for.

items.title: Student coordinates agent swarms through GitHub issues to port GTA6
items.takeaway: Amjad Masad says a high school student is recompiling GTA6 for PC, coordinating agent swarms with GitHub issues. A Hacker News post on the port reached 200 points.
items.soWhat: GitHub issues can serve as a simple shared task board for many agents on one project.

items.title: OpenRouter off-boards three inference providers after data incidents
items.takeaway: Researchers reported some providers had data compromised or broke data policies. OpenRouter dropped three, pulled 125 endpoints from zero data retention and notified customers.
items.soWhat: A model gateway does not remove the need to vet every provider behind it.

items.title: Tavi Costa: faster rate hikes risk a 2008-style deflationary bust
items.takeaway: Tavi Costa argues that accelerating rate hikes into a slowing economy dependent on easy money is how you engineer a deflationary bust like 2008, and says the Fed is doing that.
items.soWhat: If he is right, tighter money will test growth plans that rely on cheap capital.

items.title: Lean blog post on Riemann Hypothesis verification draws 1,161 HN points
items.takeaway: The Lean community blog posted 'Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis'. The Verge reported on Nov 20 that an Anthropic mathematician claims a proof with Claude.
items.soWhat: Machine-checked proofs are how claims of AI-assisted math breakthroughs get tested.

items.title: Anthropic's compute could mean 32 million tons of CO2 in 2028
items.takeaway: A Better Data Center Project case study links Anthropic's compute commitments to 32 million metric tons of CO2 in 2028; the HN title says 87% gas and 11% coal power.
items.soWhat: Power sourcing is becoming a regulatory and reputation risk for AI vendors and their buyers.
